messages:
emma: heads up — finnpay reported missing model configs in their private deployment. they saw deletes around 2025-08-01 03:15-03:45 UTC. opened INC-1851.
jinx: got it. do we have an exact window or logs yet?
emma: they gave that ~30min window. suspect either RBAC misbind or a service account rotation bleed.
akshay: quick look at the audit pipeline for org=finnpay-corp in that window. forensics-bot queued a query for config.delete / policy.modify / kms.decrypt.
forensics-bot: query: SELECT * FROM audit_events WHERE org_id='finnpay-corp' AND ts BETWEEN '2025-08-01T03:10:00Z' AND '2025-08-01T03:50:00Z' AND event_type IN ('config.delete','policy.modify','kms.decrypt') LIMIT 50;
forensics-bot: results: 12 events (6 config.delete, 3 policy.modify, 3 kms.decrypt). returning head events.
forensics-bot: #1 {ts: 2025-08-01T03:16:02Z, event_type: kms.decrypt, actor: svc-ingest-rotator@finnpay-corp, key_id: rnw-kms:keys/prd-03:v3, meta.cipher_sha: ab12...}
forensics-bot: #2 {ts: 2025-08-01T03:16:05Z, event_type: policy.modify, actor: alice-admin, policy_id: policy-rw-models, changes: grant write to svc-ingest-rotator}
lexi: pulled the config.delete payloads. sample: {ts: 2025-08-01T03:16:14Z, event_type: config.delete, actor: svc-ingest-rotator, target: model-config/finnpay-prod/llama-v2, reason: purge-stale, request_id: req-78a9} (all six look similar).
emma: so timeline is kms.decrypt -> policy.modify (grant write) -> config.delete x6. likely an automated retention job got scope-bumped.
jinx: who is alice-admin? that looks like a human admin SA.
akshay: alice-admin is an SRE automation account we created for rotations. last rotation 2025-07-30. policy-rw-models binding was changed at 03:16:05 to include svc-ingest-rotator via retention-bind-2025-07-28.
lexi: question: our audit schema buries 'reason' and 'request_id' inconsistently in meta. makes reconstruction annoying for customer deliverables. recommend promoting 'request_id' and 'intent' to top-level audit fields.
emma: I support. propose RFC: add top-level fields: actor_role, request_id, intent (enum: purge/modify/create), and key_id for kms events. also require diff payloads for policy.modify.
akshay: product will want the change staged carefully. meanwhile finnpay will expect a timeline proving this was internal retention logic. we should produce a customer-facing audit digest with: ordered events, key ids used for KMS ops, before/after policy diffs, service-account origins, and the request_ids.
jinx: I can assemble a signed digest (sha256 of the assembled timeline) and KMS-sign it with our forensics signing key, attach to INC-1851, and cc legal for disclosure wording.
emma: also recommend an immediate RBAC guard: block any policy.modify that grants write to 'models' unless target is in an allowlist. low lift, helps prevent drift.
lexi: I'll open ENG-1851-guard and add alerting for any role-binding changes that add service accounts to high-priv roles.
forensics-bot: archived payloads: gs://redwood-forensics/finnpay/2025-08-01/inc-1851.tar.gz
akshay: action items: akshay/emma draft schema RFC; lexi create guard ticket; jinx publish digest + signed proof to the incident ticket and ping legal.
jinx: will post digest by EOD and include the KMS-signature and policy diffs. will also attach the exact audit query used. :eyes: 
emma: draft customer note: short timeline, clear root cause (retention job mis-scoped due to role-binding change), confirmation that no external principal accessed keys, and attached signed audit digest.
akshay: add recommended remediation: tighten rotation scripts to avoid broad binds, require approval for retention-bind changes, and add a canary scope for purge jobs.
lexi: done — ENG-1851-guard created and assigned to eng-platform.
emma: thanks. I'll coordinate the customer message and legal review. Re-open if we find anomalies.
jinx: closing for now. will update INC-1851 when digest is uploaded.
